$doc: Tests that are RED on main and are tolerated by scripts/test-ratchet.js until their finding is closed.
This list may only ever SHRINK. The ratchet fails the build if a test not listed here fails (a regression),
and equally if a test listed here starts passing (remove it and close the finding).
Every entry carries the finding id that owns the fix, so nothing here is 'silenced' — it is queued.
Established 2026-08-02 by the Daily Improvement V3 run for S-E02-2 (PF-55 / VAL-01), the first time these
suites had ever been executed. 18 entries at establishment.
SECOND HALF, added 2026-08-12 by TOOL-13: apps.<app>.skipped records, per SUITE, how many of its tests DID
NOT EXECUTE (jest reports describe.skip and it.skip as 'pending', it.todo as 'todo'). A test that stops
running is not a failure, so it never appeared in the list above, and the gate reported '✓ no drift.' about
a check it had not performed. The two halves are deliberately asymmetric:
• failures  — an identity. A new one FAILS, and one that now passes ALSO fails (the list only shrinks).
• skipped   — a measurement. A RISE fails (a test stopped running) and a baselined suite ABSENT from the
report fails (the suite stopped existing). A FALL is REPORTED, never failed: a suite's
membership moves for legitimate reasons (someone un-skips a test, deletes an it.todo), and
failing on that would red the gate on the author who did the right thing. Check that a fall
was deliberate, then re-run --update.
Only NON-ZERO counts are recorded, so every line here means something. The cost, stated rather than hidden:
a suite with zero recorded skips that vanishes entirely is NOT caught. Catching that needs a full suite
inventory (the shape of scripts/web-route-baseline.json) and is a follow-on, not part of TOOL-13.
NO 'skipped' BLOCK IS RECORDED YET, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. It may only be written
from a COMPLETE run (--update is refused under --skip for exactly this reason), and the run that shipped
TOOL-13 could not produce one: the full apps/api suite takes ~350 s and is currently non-deterministic
(TOOL-16(b)). Inventing numbers would make the gate LOOK armed while comparing against fiction, so instead
the ratchet prints an unmissable INACTIVE warning and qualifies its own verdict line until an operator runs
`node scripts/test-ratchet.js <app> --update` from a complete run. Populating it is that operator step.
